SERVICES: MED

_patient.note:
[1] The patient is a 67-year-old female admitted from observation.
[2] The patient presented with bacteriuria.
[3] The patient has a primary diagnosis of alcoholic cirrhosis of liver with ascites.
[4] The patient has active diagnoses including alcoholic cirrhosis of liver with ascites, unspecified severe protein-calorie malnutrition, secondary esophageal varices without bleeding, portal hypertension, acquired coagulation factor deficiency, essential (primary) hypertension, other diseases of stomach and duodenum, gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis, other specified disorders of bone density and structure, unspecified site, other specified anemias, iron deficiency anemia, unspecified, and angiodysplasia of stomach and duodenum without bleeding.
[5] The patient has a past medical history of noncompliance with medication regimen, personal history of colonic polyps, personal history of nicotine dependence, and a body mass index of 24.0-24.9, adult.
[6] The patient underwent drainage of Peritoneal Cavity, Percutaneous Approach, Diagnostic.
[7] The patient underwent inspection of Upper Intestinal Tract, Via Natural or Artificial Opening Endoscopic.
[8] The patient was treated with Spironolactone 25mg PO/NG, Vitamin D 400UNIT PO/NG, Albumin 25% (12.5g / 50mL) 75g IV, Lactulose 30mL PO/NG, Ferrous Sulfate 325mg PO/NG, Calcium Carbonate 500mg PO/NG, Heparin 5000UNIT SC, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 3-10mL IV, Cholestyramine 4gm PO, Acetaminophen 650mg PO/NG, Multivitamins 1TAB PO, Ramelteon 8mg PO/NG, Docusate Sodium 100mg PO, Furosemide 40mg PO/NG, Cephalexin 500mg PO/NG, Ciprofloxacin HCl 500mg PO/NG, Rifaximin 550mg PO/NG, Bag 2BAG IV, Magnesium Sulfate 4gm IV, Ondansetron ODT 4mg PO/NG, and Omeprazole 20mg PO.
[9] The patient was admitted to the Emergency Department and Medicine wards.
[10] The patient was discharged alive to HOME.
